## Proposal and provenance

Stable algorithm slug: `recurrence-conditioned-retrieval`. Source: pm-4k6b note recorded 2026-08-03T20:40:23.212Z.

Catalog entry (26) — recurrence-conditioned retrieval priors.

Extends the catalog. Entries 1 through 25 stand unchanged and none is restated. Entries 1 through 24 score a candidate against the query. Entry 25 scores it against what this session has already been served. Entry 26 scores it against how often the situation it describes has come back.

Problem it addresses. The engine treats every recorded fact as a sample from a stationary past. A closed item that was resolved once and never returned, and a closed item belonging to a family that has returned thirty times, are indistinguishable inputs: both are terminal, both decay by recency, both carry the same edge kinds. Yet their future value to a caller is not remotely the same. The first is history. The second is a prediction. Measured on this corpus, one defect family accounts for roughly thirty closed items across eight months and returns on half of all days, and nothing in the ranking distinguishes any of its members from a one-time fix closed the same week.

The mechanism. Define a family as a set of items joined by an explicit recurrence identity. For each family, derive from the immutable record alone an occurrence count, an inter-arrival distribution over the timestamps of its members, a mean repair interval, and a trend on those inter-arrivals. From these derive a hazard: the probability that this family produces a new occurrence within the caller's horizon. The retrieval prior for any member is then raised by the family hazard, and raised further when the current request touches an artifact, file, error code or platform that the family's evidence names.

Three properties make this different from recency and from frequency. It is forward-looking rather than backward: a family whose last occurrence is old but whose period is long scores high, while a burst that has demonstrably ended decays. It is defined on the family and inherited by members, so a single old member of a live family is retrieved on the strength of its siblings, which is exactly the retrieval a caller about to repeat the defect needs. And it is asymmetric with respect to resolution quality: a family whose members were each closed with strong evidence and still returned is more informative than one closed weakly, because the recorded fixes are known not to have been sufficient.

Interaction with existing entries. It composes with the ordering-slack urgency term by supplying a second source of urgency that is not derived from the dependency graph. It composes with trust-weighted assembly by weighting a family's evidence up rather than down, which is the opposite direction and must not be folded into the same coefficient. It is strictly distinct from entry 22, lineage-aware relevance continuity: continuity follows mass through copy, split and supersede, where one thing becomes another. Recurrence follows identity through independent occurrences, where a thing happens again. It is distinct from entry 20, temporal non-stationarity mining, which detects eras in the corpus as a whole rather than periodicity within one family.

Degeneracy clauses, mandatory. On a corpus where no family has more than one member, every hazard is undefined and the term must contribute identically zero, not a small default. On a young corpus where inter-arrival estimates rest on fewer members than a declared minimum, the term must be suppressed rather than estimated from one interval, and the suppression must be visible in the explain output. On a corpus with no recurrence identities recorded at all, the entry must be a byte-identical no-op against the engine without it. Where hierarchical shrinkage from entry 21 is available, family hazards are shrunk toward the global recurrence base rate rather than trusted raw.

Blocking prerequisite. The entry is not implementable until a recurrence identity exists, which is now owned separately under the graph epic. Until then a family cannot be enumerated except by parsing titles, and a ranking signal derived from text parsing is not admissible as a scoring input.

## Delivery boundary

Evaluate this mechanism as a bounded public-SDK experiment before any production adoption. Use the existing scorer and packer contracts; no CLI-only behavior or new command noun. The historical catalog is design input, not evidence that this mechanism was implemented.

## Experiment protocol

Freeze a workspace/history revision and parameter manifest. Compare against the current deterministic SDK baseline using held-out judgments and negative controls. Report nDCG/action success, critical-evidence omission, latency p50/p95, peak memory, tokens per completed task, and rebuild cost separately. Include 3-item/minutes, real-shaped, 100k/1M-item, decades-long, and sparse/dense/imbalanced graph scenarios; smoke subsets may not claim scale acceptance. Bound candidate counts, graph expansions, elapsed time, and output size, with cancellation and completeness receipts. Record exact versus approximate behavior and approximation error; theoretical guarantees require their stated assumptions. Missing or untrusted evidence remains unknown, never inferred proof.

Promotion requires a reproducible quality improvement on the held-out target population, no regression of existing exact invariants or mandatory gates, and a declared compute/token cost justified by that improvement. Reject or defer with the same immutable evidence if those conditions fail. No production default, adaptive learning, or data export is authorized by this planning item.
